name: Question 2
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/d27538da9cf9ebb39324477a9c3e9eabd950b648507ebc616a11d5c8a6054a19.png)

The region enclosed by the curve $y={x}^{3},$ for $x\in [0,2],$ and the horizontal line $y=-1$ is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the line $y=-1,$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
worked_solution:
First, notice that we are given that the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=2$ along the $x$-axis. 

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/94d3f7e76db23c387366024bdd5dbb25f8adddc25d78bb3fc81f5900b4128fcf.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=-1,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y={x}^{3}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[\,({x}^{3})-(-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{3}+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{6}+2{x}^{3}+1)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

The region enclosed by the curve y=x3, for x∈[0,2], and the horizontal line y=−1 is rotated 360∘ about the line y=−1, as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?

a
π∫−20(2x3+1)dx
b
π∫02(x6+2x3)dx
c
π∫20(4x−x3)dx
d
π∫−20(x6+1)dx
e
π∫02(x6+2x3+1)dx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that we are given that the limits of integration are from x=0 to x=2 along the x-axis.

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the lower function y=−1, and

  • leaves through the upper function y=x3.

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

V=π∫02[(upper function)−(lower function)]2dx=π∫02[(x3)−(−1)]2dx=π∫02(x3+1)2dx=π∫02(x6+2x3+1)dx.
